The provost's office has requested a comprehensive curriculum compliance audit ahead of the upcoming accreditation review. The accreditation standards are published on a portal at http://localhost:30217 which lists the minimum structural requirements that each course must meet. Visit this portal to retrieve the current accreditation standards, and also follow the link to the content quality standards page for additional context on assessment difficulty targets.

Once the standards are retrieved, audit each course in the learning management system by counting the number of assignments, quizzes, and modules, and checking whether a syllabus has been published. Compare these counts against the accreditation thresholds from the portal to determine compliance status. A course is compliant only if it meets every structural requirement: at least 8 assignments, at least 3 quizzes, at least 4 modules, and a published syllabus. The content-quality / assessment-difficulty targets on the linked Content Quality Standards page are informational context only and must not affect the Compliant_YN determination.

Review the accreditation checklist file in the workspace for the scoring methodology and the course catalog file for reference information about the university's course offerings. Note that the learning management system is the authoritative source of courses and contains exactly 22 courses; the course_catalog.txt file is a partial, informational summary and does not list every course that must be audited.

Create an Excel file called Curriculum_Audit.xlsx with two sheets. The first sheet named "Compliance Matrix" should contain columns for Course, Assignments_Count, Quizzes_Count, Modules_Count, Has_Syllabus (Yes or No), Compliant_YN (Yes if all standards are met, No otherwise), and Issues (a semicolon-separated list of specific deficiencies, or "None" if compliant). Include all 22 courses sorted alphabetically by course name. The second sheet named "Summary" should contain rows for Total_Courses, Compliant_Courses, Non_Compliant_Courses, and Compliance_Rate (as a percentage).

Also create a Word document called Audit_Report.docx containing a narrative compliance report. The document should include an executive summary describing the overall compliance rate and key findings, a section detailing the most common areas of non-compliance, and recommendations for bringing non-compliant courses into alignment before the accreditation review.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, resolve the shared context sources in the main agent, score every course with one Explore agent that owns all four metric reads, and write both artifacts directly from the frozen canonical payload. Canvas is read-only.

Before Wave 1, the main agent resolves the task-visible workspace directory from the runtime allowed-directory listing (or the literal accessible-workspace directory already supplied by the harness), freezes it as `<workspace_root>`, and rejects bare `/workspace` and dumps/run-specific paths. In one native-parallel response it then snapshots `http://localhost:30217` once (freezing `min_assignments=8, min_quizzes=3, min_modules=4, syllabus_required`), snapshots `http://localhost:30217/standards.html` once (content-quality context, informational only), reads `<workspace_root>/accreditation_checklist.md` completely (binary scoring rule: every requirement must pass), reads `<workspace_root>/course_catalog.txt` completely (partial, informational only), and calls `canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true)` once, requiring the 22 unique task-visible courses exactly as enumerated below and freezing the exact `{course_id,course_code,course_name}` manifest. If count or identity is missing/duplicated, stop rather than guessing.

Task: Retrieve accreditation standards from a local web portal.

Context: A university provost's office needs the current accreditation standards for a curriculum compliance audit. A portal is running at http://localhost:30217. Its main page lists the minimum structural requirements that each course must meet (thresholds such as minimum numbers of assignments, quizzes, modules, and syllabus publication requirements). The main page also contains a link to a "Content Quality Standards" page (wording may vary slightly) that describes assessment difficulty targets — informational context only.

Steps:
1. Use the playwright browser tools: browser_navigate to http://localhost:30217.
2. Use browser_snapshot (navigate through all spans if the content is long; use browser_snapshot_search if needed) and extract the FULL text of the page: title, every listed structural/accreditation requirement with its exact numeric threshold.
3. Locate the link on that page to the Content Quality Standards page and navigate to it (click it or navigate directly to its URL).
4. Extract the FULL text of that second page as well (assessment difficulty targets, any tables or percentages).

Deliverables (report back):
- The complete verbatim text of the main accreditation standards page, including every numeric threshold.
- The complete verbatim text of the Content Quality Standards page.
- The URLs of both pages.

This is read-only: do not submit forms or mutate anything; just browse and report.
Fetch accreditation standards portal

Task: Read-only structural audit of ALL courses in the Canvas LMS. The LMS contains exactly 22 courses and every one of them must be audited.

For EACH course, collect four data points:
1. Number of assignments — use canvas_list_assignments(course_id). If the result is paginated, count assignments across all pages.
2. Number of quizzes — use canvas_list_quizzes(course_id). Follow pagination if present.
3. Number of modules — use canvas_list_modules(course_id). Follow pagination if present.
4. Published syllabus — use canvas_get_syllabus(course_id) (fall back to the syllabus_body field from canvas_get_course if needed). A non-empty syllabus body counts as Yes; empty, null, or whitespace-only counts as No. Note that a syllabus saying something like "no syllabus available" should still be evaluated on whether real syllabus content exists — report the actual syllabus body text (or a short excerpt) for any borderline cases so I can judge.

How to find all 22 courses:
1. First try canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true). Fetch all pages if pagination is present.
2. If fewer than 22 distinct courses are returned, use account-level listing: canvas_get_account(1), canvas_list_sub_accounts(account_id), and canvas_list_account_courses(account_id, ...) across accounts until you have exactly 22 distinct courses in total.
3. Verify the final distinct course count is exactly 22; report the count.

Deliverable (report back): a single compact table covering ALL 22 courses, sorted alphabetically by course name, with columns:
course_id | course_name | course_code | assignments_count | quizzes_count | modules_count | has_syllabus (Yes/No)

Also report: the total number of distinct courses found, and any anomalies (API errors, pagination issues, courses excluded because they are deleted, etc.).

Strict constraint: READ-ONLY. Do not create, update, delete, enroll, submit, or message anything in Canvas. Only list/get/read operations.
Audit all Canvas courses counts

Task: Create a Word document at this exact path using the word MCP tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, add_table, insert_numbered_list_near_text, highlight_table_header):

/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-canvas-curriculum-audit/workspace/Audit_Report.docx

IMPORTANT: A file may already exist at that path (an empty document shell). Overwrite/recreate it so the final document contains EXACTLY the structure below, in this exact order. Add elements sequentially in the order given (each tool call appends to the end of the document). Document metadata: title "Curriculum Compliance Audit Report".

Build the document with these elements in order:

1. Heading level 1: "Curriculum Compliance Audit Report"

2. Paragraph (normal): "This report presents the findings of a curriculum compliance audit of all 22 courses hosted in the university's Learning Management System (LMS), conducted at the request of the Provost's Office ahead of the upcoming accreditation review. Each course was evaluated against the structural requirements published on the University Accreditation Standards Portal: a minimum of 8 assignments, a minimum of 3 quizzes, a minimum of 4 modules, and a published syllabus. Course-by-course results are provided in the accompanying workbook, Curriculum_Audit.xlsx."

3. Heading level 2: "Executive Summary"

4. Paragraph: "Of the 22 courses audited, 11 (50.0%) satisfy every structural requirement and are considered compliant; the remaining 11 courses (50.0%) are non-compliant on at least one requirement. Syllabus publication is the institution's strongest control: all 22 courses have an active, published syllabus, so no course fails this criterion. The deficiencies are concentrated entirely in course structure. Missing quizzes and insufficient assignments are the most common failures, each affecting 9 of 22 courses (41%); inadequate module organization affects 7 of 22 courses (32%)."

5. Paragraph: "At the subject level the pattern is stark. Foundations of Finance (4 of 4 offerings), Global Governance & Geopolitics (3 of 3), and Creative Computing & Culture (2 of 2) are fully compliant, while Biochemistry & Bioinformatics is compliant in 2 of 4 offerings. Conversely, every offering of Applied Analytics & Algorithms (0 of 2), Data-Driven Design (0 of 4), and Environmental Economics & Ethics (0 of 3) fails at least one structural standard. Five courses fail all three structural counts at once: both Applied Analytics & Algorithms offerings (Fall 2013, Fall 2014) and three of the four Data-Driven Design offerings (Fall 2013, Fall 2014, Spring 2014)."

6. Heading level 2: "Accreditation Standards Applied"

7. Paragraph: "The audit applies the Course Structure Requirements published on the University Accreditation Standards Portal: (1) at least 8 graded assignments per course; (2) at least 3 quizzes for formative assessment; (3) course content organized into at least 4 modules; and (4) an active syllabus published and accessible to students. The linked Content Quality Standards additionally define assessment difficulty targets: average assignment scores of 60 to 85, a minimum quiz pass rate of 70%, and a minimum module completion rate of 80%. In line with the accreditation checklist, these content-quality targets are informational context only and were not used in the compliant determination, which rests solely on the four structural requirements above."

8. Heading level 2: "Most Common Areas of Non-Compliance"

9. Paragraph (bold the leading phrase if convenient): "Insufficient quizzes (9 courses). The most common deficiency, tied with assignments, is the lack of quizzes. Eight of the affected courses contain no quizzes at all, and Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013) contains only one. Affected courses span all offerings of Data-Driven Design, Environmental Economics & Ethics, and Applied Analytics & Algorithms, plus Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014)."

10. Paragraph: "Insufficient graded assignments (9 courses). Nine courses fall below the 8-assignment minimum. The Environmental Economics & Ethics offerings are the most acute, with only 5 assignments each (3 short of the standard); Applied Analytics & Algorithms (both terms) and Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014) have 6; and the Data-Driven Design offerings of Fall 2013, Fall 2014, and Spring 2014 have 7."

11. Paragraph: "Inadequate module organization (7 courses). Seven courses contain fewer than 4 modules. All four Data-Driven Design offerings are organized into a single module, as is Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2013); both Applied Analytics & Algorithms offerings contain 3 modules each."

12. Paragraph: "Syllabus publication (0 deficiencies). All 22 courses publish an active syllabus; this requirement is fully met across the institution."

13. Heading level 2: "Non-Compliant Courses in Detail"

14. Paragraph: "The table below lists the 11 non-compliant courses and their specific structural deficiencies."

15. A table (12 rows x 2 columns) with this data (row 1 is the header):
Header row: ["Course", "Deficiencies"]
["Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013)", "6 assignments (minimum 8); 1 quiz (minimum 3); 3 modules (minimum 4)"]
["Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014)", "6 assignments (minimum 8); 0 quizzes (minimum 3); 3 modules (minimum 4)"]
